name: Display LUT after the film output: one 33³ half-float tap in the last pass
summary:
This design builds on the plan that already exists, plans/handover-grade-editor.md (its brief, its "plan so far" and open questions 1-5), and it is the display-lut design of plans/grade-editor/design-workflow.js. No worktree switch is needed. C:/projects/WIDE_3d-flatform/.claude/worktrees/sbb-colour-matching is already on sbb/grade-editor at HEAD 81ccfab. That commit is 2def41d plus the handover files under plans/ only. Implementation commits go on top of 81ccfab, and .claude/launch.json stays uncommitted.

The idea:
- tone-mapping.ts stays exactly as it is.
- The whole grade (except exposure) is baked on the CPU into one 33³ RGBA16F Data3DTexture.
- The LUT is sampled once per pixel, in display (sRGB-encoded) space, after three's renderOutput (film, then OETF) and before the canvas write.
- The tap therefore sees exactly what a screenshot shows, so a .cube made on a grade-off screenshot in Resolve or Photoshop applies 1:1, up to trilinear interpolation.

One implementation for both output paths:
- depth-of-field.ts gets setGrade(). It re-wraps only the final output node: outputColorTransform=false and outputNode = grade.tap(renderOutput(chain)). It does not rebuild DoF or EDL.
- While a grade is compiled in, the no-post path (DoF and EDL off) also goes through the same RenderPipeline. That is the same pass count as renderer.render: scene into a HalfFloat target, then one quad.
- So the grade works with every tone curve, with the tone stage off, and on WebGPU, WebGL2 and phones.
- When it is off, the graph and shader are byte-identical to today, and the cost is zero.

Editor and data flow:
- The editor is a new "Grade" section in Design, with tabs Primaries / Curves / Hue / Split / Look and canvas widgets (wheels, curves, hue curves).
- The bake runs in a module worker and is latest-wins. Measured with a node prototype: 7.5 ms at 33³ with every control on, 2.35 ms at 17³.
- A before/after split is one uniform compare in the same shader, with a DOM drag handle.
- Other tools: stills with A/B, undo/redo, presets, .cube import/export, a "Frame (grade off)" PNG for authoring, and Copy values plus Paste values for a config-shaped `grade:` block.

Compile-in policy:
- The grade is compiled in when it is enabled AND (it is not identity, OR a look is loaded, OR the Grade section is open).
- The decision is made only on commit or section open/close, never on an 'input' event, so a drag never triggers a recompile.

Pure modules, tested under node --test:
- grade-model.ts
- grade-bake.ts
- cube-format.ts

All three are free of three and DOM imports.

name: Unified scene-referred grade stage (Canopy Log residual LUT) with an optional display look slot
summary:
This design builds on the plan that already exists: plans/handover-grade-editor.md (open questions 1 to 5) and plans/grade-editor/design-workflow.js, where this is the "unified" angle. No worktree switch was needed. C:/projects/WIDE_3d-flatform/.claude/worktrees/sbb-colour-matching is already on sbb/grade-editor. Its HEAD is 81ccfab, which is 2def41d plus the plans/ files only. Nothing was edited.

THE IDEA
- The film's tone part (luma log contrast and saturation) and its warm/cool split stop being hand-written film parts. They become controls of one grade, together with every editor control.
- The grade is baked on the CPU into one 33^3 RGBA16F LUT and sampled once per pixel inside the existing film tone-mapping function.
- The grade sits before the shoulder, so it sees HDR scene-linear values.
- Exposure, shoulder (highlight roll-off), black lift and vignette stay analytic, as live uniforms.
- The film look becomes the editor's default preset: a GradeState in config.ts.

THREE THINGS MAKE IT WORK (all measured in node; scripts in the scratchpad unified/ folder)
1. A residual LUT. The LUT stores G(x) - x in scene-linear half floats, and the shader adds it back to x.
   - Neutral then means a residual of exactly 0, so identity is bit-exact even while compiled in.
   - Smooth grades interpolate far better this way than storing the encoded output. For the film preset at 33^3:
     - full cube: 1.4 LSB max instead of 6.2;
     - sand: 0.8 instead of 6.1;
     - lit canopy: 0.5 instead of 1.4.
2. "Canopy Log", a log2 shaper with a C1 linear toe that maps 0 to exactly 0.
   - Toe at 2^-5, top at 16 linear: 10.44 stops over 32 cells.
   - Positions: black at 0, 18 % grey at s 0.380, diffuse white 1.0 at 0.617, white point 2 at 0.713.
   - In the shader it is branch-free: s = min(x*K, (log2(max(x, toe)) - A) / B).
3. Homogeneous extrapolation above the lattice. With q = max(peak/16, 1), the shader computes out = x + q*R(x/q).
   - This keeps the sun, cloud tops and the 4.7x matched basemap graded with the right hue.
   - Without it, sky x20 is 31 LSB off; with it, 0.7 LSB.

MATCH TO TODAY'S LOOK
- The film preset matches the analytic film to at most 1.3 LSB on every set measured: canopy, lit canopy, matched basemap, sand, sky (including x20), fog cream, cloud tops, and the full cube including x10. This includes 8-bit filter weights.
- 1.5 to 8 % of 8-bit codes move by one level.
- It is not bit-exact. That needs the user's visual sign-off.

THE BIGGEST MEASURED WEAKNESS: SCREENSHOT .cube FILES
- A .cube made on a screenshot cannot be folded into the scene-referred LUT. Going through the inverse display transform costs 14 to 25 LSB.
- The film's 0.01 lift floor clips 19 to 24 % of the outputs of Adobe's film-emulation cubes.
- So an imported .cube goes into a second, display-referred "Look" slot after the film output. It is compiled in only while a cube is loaded, and it applies 1:1 like the display design.

WHAT IS GAINED
- One model and one place for the whole look: presets, snapshots, A/B and Copy values all work on one state.
- A professional structure: grade in log, then the output transform. Gains, warm highlights and curves act on real HDR data and roll off through the shoulder instead of clipping at 1.
- One implementation for both output paths. It lives in the tone fn, so it works on the DoF/EDL post quad and on the plain renderer output alike.
- The GPU cost does not grow with the number of controls.
- A before/after compare that is nearly free: the two sides share the shoulder, lift and vignette.

WHAT IS NOT GAINED
- "Fewer ALU ops" does not hold. The tap path costs 3 log2 plus one 3D tap, against today's 2 transcendentals plus about 35 flops.
- The lattice spends about 38 % of its cells above diffuse white, so strong grades interpolate worse than a display LUT does in the visible range: a pro grade measures 0.7 LSB on canopy, 2.6 on basemap and 4.2 on the full cube at 33^3.

name: Editor-first: a colourist's grade on a display LUT, baked progressively in a worker
summary:
This design builds on plans/handover-grade-editor.md and answers its open questions 1-5. The worktree is already on sbb/grade-editor. HEAD is 81ccfab, which is 2def41d plus the plans/ handover only, so no switch is needed, and the implementation commits on top of 81ccfab.

PLACEMENT: one display-referred 3D-LUT tap, appended after renderOutput in the single app-owned final quad.
- The LUT sees exactly what the screen shows (the film output, sRGB-encoded), so a .cube graded on a screenshot applies 1:1.
- The before/after split is a free select in the same shader.
- The grade works with every tone curve and with the tone stage off.
- While the grade is compiled in, both output paths run through the same RenderPipeline (path B, DoF and EDL off, is routed through it), so there is ONE implementation.
- Off or neutral, with the editor closed, the output graph is today's, byte for byte.

STATE: one LookState = { tone (curve, exposure, film parts), grade (the LUT-baked controls), lut (an imported cube + amount) }.
- It drives undo/redo, A/B snapshots, presets (Film Warm, Neutral, later Evergreen) and Copy values that pastes back.
- The film stays analytic and bit-exact. The editor controls it through handles, not by re-implementing it.

LUT: RGBA16F, linear-filtered, values stored unclamped (the 8-bit canvas clamps per pixel).
- Own lattice: 33³. A neutral bake is exactly i/32 at every node (measured 0 of 35,937 off).
- Imported cube: the lattice becomes the smallest integer refinement k·(N−1)+1 ≥ 33 of the cube's own grid. Measured on the 99 unique 3D cubes Adobe ships on this PC:
  - with that refinement, 21³ cubes reproduce their native trilinear result within 0.10 LSB (half storage only);
  - resampled onto 33³ instead, they are off by up to 15 LSB and 23 % of 8-bit outputs change.
  So "loads as is" is only true with the refinement.

BAKE: in a module worker, latest-wins, one job in flight.
- While a control is dragged it bakes every 2nd node (17³ of 33³) and fills the rest multilinearly. That is exactly what a 17³ texture would render (measured 0.09 LSB, half storage).
- On release it does the full bake.
- Measured in node 24 on this desktop: draft about 1.3 ms, full 33³ about 5.3 ms (5.0 ms evaluation + 0.25 ms Float16Array pack).

COMPILE-IN: compiledIn = switch AND (editor open OR grade non-identity). It is decided only on discrete events (switch, section open/close, release, preset, snapshot, import, paste, undo), never on 'input', so no drag ever recompiles.

UI: a tabbed "Colour grade" section in the Design panel (Primaries · Curves · Hue · Tones · LUT).
- Canvas widgets: draggable-point curves, relative-drag wheels like Resolve's, periodic hue curves.
- A draggable compare line, a frame-grab button that exports the frame with the grade bypassed, .cube import/export and paste-back.
- On phones: a peek mode that clears the bottom sheet while dragging, so the frame is visible.

GPU cost: one trilinear 3D tap plus about 6 ALU ops per pixel while compiled in, nothing when out. This is still to be measured with the stopped-loop timestamp method.
